title: Tracing an LR(1) Parser with State Items and Lookaheads
description: Step through a table-driven LR(1) parser while inspecting the exact LR(1) items in each state on top of the stack.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `PROD` numbers the three grammar rules: `1: S -> X y x`, `2: X -> x X`, and `3: X -> y`. `ITEMS` records the LR(1) items for states `0` through `7`. `ACTION` and `GOTO` encode the shift, reduce, accept, and nonterminal transitions.

`parse(text)` maintains alternating symbols and state numbers on `stack` (starting at `[0]`). Each iteration prints `ITEMS[state]` and looks up `act = ACTION.get((state, tok))`. `'s...'` shifts `tok` and pushes the next state (lines 31-33). `'r...'` pops `2 * len(rhs)` entries and pushes `lhs` followed by `GOTO[(stack[-1], lhs)]` (lines 35-37).

A reduction rewinds the stack on lines 35-37. Each shifted symbol pushed two stack elements (`tok` and `state`). Thus, `del stack[-2 * len(rhs):]` uncovers the state that was on top before `rhs` began. `GOTO[(stack[-1], lhs)]` transitions from that state on `lhs`.
Lines 39-42 run `parse` on two inputs: `"xxyyx"` and `"xyx"`.

steps.question: When `parse("xyx")` shifts `'x'` into state 3 and `'y'` into state 4 (`[X -> y ., y]`), the next input token is `'x'`. What does `ACTION.get((4, 'x'))` return, and why?
steps.answer: It returns `None` and prints `ERROR: no item expects x`. State 4's item `[X -> y ., y]` only reduces `X -> y` when the lookahead is `'y'`.

steps.description: While parsing `"xxyyx"`, state 4 sees lookahead `'y'` and executes `r3` (`X -> y`). It pops `['y', 4]` on line 36 before `GOTO[(3, 'X')]` pushes state `6`.
